key_insight: Water dissociation on g-C3N4 nanosheets markedly improves optical absorbance and electrical conductance, making the material more promising for photocatalytic water splitting.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a multiscale computational basis for screening and optimizing g-C3N4-based photocatalysts for sustainable hydrogen production.
method: DFT calculations benchmarked the electronic and optical properties of pristine and water-adsorbed g-C3N4.
SCC-DFTB simulations examined OH/H2O adsorption effects on nanosheet behavior.
ReaxFF molecular dynamics modeled multiple H2O emissions and estimated H2 evolution trends.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a comparative computational evaluation showing stronger absorbance and conductance after H2O dissociation into HO and O relative to the pristine nanosheet.
watch_item: Because the conclusions are based on atomistic simulations, real-world photocatalytic performance may differ under defects, temperature, solvent, and experimental surface conditions.
paper_title: Computational Study of Water Adsorption and Dissociative Mechanisms Impacting g-C3N4's Optical and Electronic Properties
